header.title: Adversus Mathematicos: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Sextus Empiricus
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg0544.tlg002.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

nodes.text: (for it is an observation of phenomena, like farming and navigation, from which one can foretell droughts and heavy rains, plagues and earthquakes, and other such changes in the surrounding air), but against the casting of nativities, which the Chaldaeans adorn with grander names, proclaiming themselves 'mathematicians' and 'astrologers'; they abuse life in many ways, raise a great superstition against us like a fortress, and allow us to do nothing according to right reason.
